name: 8.6 Hypothesis Testing of a Single Mean and Single Proportion
_note: Built 2026-08-12. All eleven authored (q53-lab-name-the-distribution, q54-tv-test-statistic, q55-tv-decision-and-conclusion, q56-language-condition-check, q57-language-test-statistic, q58-language-decision-and-conclusion, q59-jeans-test-statistic, q60-jeans-wrong-curve, q61-lab-honesty-check, q70-lab-state-the-hypotheses, pre-frq-grade-a-lab-hypothesis-test) = eleven. Points 9x10 + 10 = 100 (rebalanced from the SPEC's 110 on 2026-08-14 to the every-assignment-is-100 rule; lab pre-FRQs are 10 points per the 4.4-7.4 labs). BookSHelf 8.6 is a LAB: three complete hypothesis tests on data the class collects itself - the Television Survey (one mean, sigma = 2 known, normal), the Language Survey (one proportion, claimed 42.3%, normal-for-a-proportion), and the Jeans Survey (one mean, sigma unknown, n = 8, Student t with df = 7). Every answer is deterministic from the section's own Try It Now demonstrations (TV: SE 0.3651, z -2.19, p 0.0142, reject; Language: np0 10.575, nq0 14.425, p' 0.56, SE 0.0988, z 1.39, p 0.165, do not reject; Jeans: SE 0.2687, t 1.86, p 0.053, do not reject, wrong-curve p 0.031). Pre-FRQ is authored-first (no lab FRQ to mirror; the 8.1-8.5 pre-FRQs are claimed): categories State the Hypotheses (3) / Run the Test (4) / Write the Conclusion (3), dropped category RUN THE TEST (a plausible answer states the hypotheses and writes a conclusion for a given result without ever computing the test statistic). This is DIFFERENT from the 4.4/4.6/5.3/6.4 lab pre-FRQs' dropped categories (State the Theoretical Value / State the Empirical Value / Compare and Explain the Gap) and from 7.1-7.4's (Confidence Level Meaning / Assessing the Claim / Statistical Decision / Build the Interval) and 8.1-8.5's (Real-World Example / Name the Probabilities / Check the Conditions / Interpretation of Evidence / Test stat + p-value).
